name: GRENADA
lead: Grenada is a small Caribbean island country. You could drive around it in a few hours. Yet its nutmeg fills kitchens all over the world. Rainforest mountains slope down to coral reefs, and candy-coloured houses line the harbours.
geo: A sleeping volcano forms the island's spine, covered in rainforest. Grand Etang Lake fills an old crater 530 m up. Tree ferns and mist ring its still water.
The capital, St. George's, curves around a horseshoe harbour. A tunnel cut through solid rock in 1894 still carries cars today.
animals: Mona monkeys swing through the trees at Grand Etang. Slave ships brought their ancestors from West Africa around 1760. Now they beg bananas from hikers.
Leatherback turtles bury their eggs on Levera Beach by moonlight each spring. The Grenada dove lives nowhere else on Earth.
culture: Spicemas is Grenada's August carnival. It starts at 4 a.m. Jab Jab dancers cover themselves in black oil and chains. They turn an old insult into pride.
Oildown is the national dish. Breadfruit, coconut milk, callaloo (leafy greens) and salted meat simmer in one pot. Big Drum music fills village festivals.
history: Carib people called the island Camerhogne. Columbus spotted it in 1498. The French settled in 1649, and Britain took over in 1783.
Grenada won independence on 7 February 1974. In 1983 US troops landed during a political crisis. It was the only modern American invasion of a Caribbean country.
wows: Grenada grows about 20% of the world’s nutmeg.
The world's first underwater sculpture park lies off Molinere Bay, with 65 statues just 5 m down.
Grenada is the only country with a spice on its flag: a nutmeg.
Mona monkeys come from West Africa, yet have lived wild in Grenada’s rainforest for over 260 years.
The St. George’s road tunnel was hand-drilled in 1894 and is still in daily use.
Leatherback turtles, which nest on Grenada’s beaches, are the biggest turtles alive.
One nutmeg tree makes two spices, nutmeg and mace.

myths.myth: Grenada and the Grenadines are the same place
myths.fact: The Grenadines are small islands, and most belong to St Vincent. Grenada owns just the southern ones, like Carriacou.

myths.myth: Nutmeg trees give fruit in their first year
myths.fact: A nutmeg tree needs 7 to 9 years for its first fruit. A full harvest takes up to 20 years.
